items.title: The Similars
items.reason: Eight strangers are stranded in a remote bus station during a worldwide storm and progressively confront seizures, identical-face transformations, an impossible barrier preventing escape and competing explanations ranging from infection and government action to the supernatural. The film keeps changing the working explanation: the transformations spread, Ulises appears to be the source, the station becomes physically impossible to leave, Ignacio's comic-book scenario becomes relevant, and the final discoveries identify Ignacio as the reality-altering agent and connect the phenomenon to an impossible external influence. Contemporary whole-film reviews specifically describe an arsenal of twists, sustained paranoia and several additional turns that keep the feature-length premise moving. Its deliberately 1960s-styled monochrome presentation and substantial horror content are meaningful negatives, but the central anomaly, containment, unknown rules, suspense and repeated reframing remain dominant across the runtime.
